symptom: go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver v1 stayed on a customer's blocking dependency scan (CVE-2026-107325) with no fix available on the v1 line ever — v1.17.10 is its last release and the module is deprecated. Dropping it meant moving 107 non-test and 179 test files off v1 bson, through the BSON serialization core
cause: v1 and v2 decode nested documents into DIFFERENT Go types, and the type assertions mxcli reads them back with were written against v1. Measured on identical bytes: destination bson.D nests primitive.D under v1 and bson.D under v2 (equivalent, no action); destination bson.M nests primitive.M under v1 and bson.D under v2 (BREAKS `doc[k].(bson.M)`); destination map[string]any nests map[string]any under v1 and bson.D under v2 (BREAKS `doc[k].(map[string]any)`). A failed type assertion is not an error, so the value is silently dropped and the next write emits a document with a property missing — unmergeable in Studio Pro (canon.CompletePropertySets, #1373). v2 also removed bson.D.Map()
file: `modelsdk/bsoncompat/unmarshal.go` (new leaf package: UnmarshalDocM, UnmarshalDocMap, DMap), 294 files repointed at v2, `go.mod`/`go.sum` v1 requirement dropped
insight: Do NOT audit the type assertions — 618 of them in the migrated files, and a wrong one compiles clean. v2's decoder already has the switch: `Decoder.DefaultDocumentM()` restores v1's nested-bson.M and `DefaultDocumentMap()` restores v1's nested-map[string]any, both at every depth including inside arrays. That turns a 1-2 day assertion audit into 2 helpers plus 73 mechanical call-site swaps (39 bson.M destinations + 34 map[string]any), found by grepping each file for how its Unmarshal target was DECLARED, not by reading the call. The two helpers are NOT interchangeable: bson.M is a named type (type M map[string]any), so a bson.M value fails `.(map[string]any)` and vice versa — mdl/executor's TestResolveWebServiceName_ReadsMapDecodedDocuments exists because that exact confusion already cost a debugging round, and it caught this migration too (it pins its own precondition, so it reports "this test no longer pins the trap it was written for" rather than passing vacuously — copy that pattern). bson.D destinations need NO helper, and applying one there re-introduces the bug inverted. Placement is load-bearing: the helpers cannot live in modelsdk/codec, which imports modelsdk/mpr, which imports canon and meta — whose own tests then could not import codec ("import cycle not allowed in test"); a leaf package depending only on the driver is the only placement every layer can use. Mechanically: the rewrite is a script (284 files in minutes), and the only real breakage is files that imported BOTH drivers with v2 aliased — they end up with two identical imports. Guard against regression with a test that walks the tree for the v1 import AND reads go.mod, since re-adding either is not a build error; verified by control (names the file and the go.mod line). go mod tidy cannot run in this repo at all — mdl/exprcheck/roundtrip_test.go, //go:build roundtrip, imports the long-deleted mdl/backend/mpr — so the requirement was dropped with `go mod edit -droprequire` plus a manual go.sum prune, proven by `go version -m bin/mxcli` showing only v2
